hypotheses: Prior attempts retained integer midpoint temporaries. Reusing float endpoint temporaries for the midpoint shortens the integer live ranges and removes the four-byte displacement of the second bias relocation.

Reusing the effect scalar for its narrowed color value changes interference with the special flag. This restores the special flag to retail r31 and, in combination with float midpoint reuse, restores all endpoint and midpoint load/store ordering.
Ordering scalar declarations by the observed FPR interference improves the register mapping. Final float declaration order x2,z1,y1,x1,y2,z2 produces the best measured result.
